label: archaeal-type flagellum
definition: A non-membrane-bounded archaeal motility organelle, also called the archaellum, whose ATP-powered membrane motor rotates one or more glycosylated type-IV-pilin-like archaellin filaments outside the cell to drive swimming.

label: attachment organelle
definition: A membrane-bounded polar cell extension in Mycoplasma species that concentrates cytadherence and cytoskeletal proteins for host-cell attachment, gliding motility, and organelle-linked cell division.

label: bacterial-type flagellum
definition: The rotary motility organelle of bacteria: a long helical filament of flagellin joined by a flexible hook to a basal body that spans the cell envelope. The basal body houses a rotor (MS and C rings) driven by membrane-embedded stator units that convert ion flow (H+ or Na+) into torque; the flagellar type III export apparatus at its base secretes the axial subunits. Not homologous to the archaeal archaellum or the eukaryotic cilium.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body
definition: The basal cell-envelope substructure of a bacterial flagellum, consisting of a rod, a series of rings, Mot stator proteins, the switch complex, and the proximal flagellum-specific type III export apparatus.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, C ring
definition: The cytoplasmic FliG/FliM/FliN switch ring of the bacterial flagellar basal body, assembled on the MS ring to form the rotor face that receives torque from Mot/Pom stator units and changes rotational bias in response to phosphorylated CheY.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, distal rod
definition: The portion of the central rod of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body that is distal to the cell membrane; spans most of the distance between the inner and outer membranes.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, distal rod, L ring
definition: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; anchors the basal body to the outer membrane.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, distal rod, P ring
definition: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; anchors the basal body to the peptidoglycan layer.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, MS ring
definition: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; a double-flanged ring that anchors the basal body to the cytoplasmic membrane.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, proximal rod
definition: The portion of the central rod of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body that is proximal to the cell membrane; the proximal rod connects the distal rod to the flagellar motor.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, rod
definition: The central portion of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body, which spans the periplasm and threads through the rings.

label: bacterial-type flagellum filament
definition: The long (approximately 20 nm), thin external structure of the bacterial-type flagellum, which acts as a propeller.

label: bacterial-type flagellum hook
definition: The portion of the bacterial-type flagellum that connects the filament to the basal body.

label: bacterial-type flagellum hook-filament junction
definition: The FlgK/FlgL hook-associated protein junction at the distal end of the bacterial-type flagellar hook that couples the flexible hook to the flagellin filament and buffers mechanical stress while initiating filament assembly.

label: bacterial-type flagellum motor
definition: A bacterial flagellar basal-body motor composed of an MS-ring/C-ring rotor complex and one or more Mot/Pom-family stator complexes in the cytoplasmic membrane that convert ion flow into rotary torque and bias clockwise or counterclockwise output.

label: bacterial-type flagellum rotor complex
definition: The bacterial flagellar basal-body rotor built from the membrane-anchored FliF MS ring and the cytoplasmic FliG/FliM/FliN C ring, which together receive torque from stator units, rotate the axial rod, and bias clockwise or counterclockwise motor output.

label: bacterial-type flagellum secretion apparatus
definition: A flagellum-specific type III export apparatus at the cytoplasmic side of the bacterial MS ring that uses a FlhA/FlhB/FliP/FliQ/FliR membrane export gate and a FliH/FliI/FliJ cytoplasmic ATPase complex to export rod, hook, and filament subunits through the growing flagellum.

label: bacterial-type flagellum stator complex
definition: An ion-driven membrane complex in the bacterial flagellar motor, typically with five A subunits surrounding two B subunits, that transduces proton or sodium flow into torque on the flagellar rotor and anchors to the cell wall through the B subunits.

label: curli
definition: Extracellular amyloid fibers assembled from CsgA by the Csg secretion and nucleation machinery that form a pilus subtype in enteric biofilm matrices.

label: periplasmic flagellum
definition: A bacterial-type flagellar appendage of spirochetes whose filaments reside in the periplasmic space between the cytoplasmic and outer membranes, attach near the cell poles, and rotate to deform the cell cylinder for motility.

label: type IV pilus
definition: A dynamic bacterial surface filament assembled from type IV pilins by an inner-membrane ATPase machinery. Reversible extension and retraction can generate force for twitching motility, adhesion, surface sensing, and DNA uptake.

label: MreB filament
definition: The actin-like cytoskeletal filament of rod-shaped bacteria. MreB polymerises into short membrane-associated filaments that circle the cell at an angle to its long axis and move processively around it, carrying the elongasome — the peptidoglycan synthases that widen the sidewall — so that new wall material is inserted where the filaments travel. It is a homologue of eukaryotic actin by fold, not by sequence identity.

label: divisome complex
definition: The membrane-associated protein machine that constricts a dividing bacterial cell. It is organised by the FtsZ ring — treadmilling filaments of the tubulin homologue FtsZ tethered to the inner membrane — which positions and moves the septal peptidoglycan synthases that build the division septum.

label: elongasome
definition: The sidewall peptidoglycan-synthesis machine of rod-shaped bacteria, also called the Rod complex. A SEDS-family glycosyltransferase (RodA) works with a class B penicillin-binding protein (PBP2) to polymerise and crosslink new wall material into the cylinder, while MreC, MreD and RodZ couple the complex to MreB filaments, which distribute it around the circumference. It is the elongation counterpart of the divisome.

label: phycobilisome
definition: A membrane-associated light-harvesting pigment-protein complex of cyanobacteria and red algae, built from phycobiliprotein core and rod cylinders plus linker polypeptides, that funnels phycobilin excitation energy to photosynthetic reaction centers.

label: proton-transporting ATP synthase complex
definition: The rotary motor enzyme that makes ATP from ADP and phosphate using the ion motive force across the membrane. It has two coupled sectors: a membrane-embedded Fo, whose c-ring turns as protons cross it, and a soluble F1 (alpha3beta3gammadeltaepsilon), whose catalytic beta subunits are driven through their conformational cycle by the rotating gamma subunit.

label: cell outer membrane
definition: The outermost lipid bilayer of a diderm cell envelope. In canonical Gram-negative bacteria it is asymmetric, with phospholipid enriched in the inner leaflet and lipopolysaccharide enriched in the outer leaflet, and contains beta-barrel proteins that mediate transport and assembly.

label: Gram-negative-bacterium-type cell wall
definition: The relatively thin peptidoglycan layer of a Gram-negative cell envelope, located in the periplasm between the cytoplasmic and outer membranes and physically connected to the outer membrane by lipoproteins.

label: peptidoglycan-based cell wall
definition: A protective, load-bearing structure outside the cytoplasmic membrane, built from glycan strands of alternating N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid cross-linked by short peptides. The resulting murein sacculus surrounds the cell and resists turgor pressure.

label: S-layer
definition: A paracrystalline monomolecular array of one or more (glyco)protein species that self-assemble on the outermost surface of the cell envelope, with oblique, square or hexagonal lattice symmetry. S-layers are common in Archaea, where they are often the sole wall component, and widespread but patchily distributed in Bacteria.

label: gas vesicle
definition: A gas-filled, non-membrane-bounded protein organelle, usually shaped as a cylindrical shell with conical end caps. Its gas-permeable, water-excluding wall lowers cell density and enables buoyancy regulation in aquatic microbes.

label: gas vesicle shell
definition: The proteinaceous structure surrounding a gas vesicle.

label: acidocalcisome
definition: An acidic electron-dense membrane-bounded organelle found in diverse microbes that stores polyphosphate, pyrophosphate, calcium and other cations and uses proton pumps and cation transporters to maintain its ion-rich matrix.

label: anammoxosome
definition: A ladderane-lipid-bounded intracytoplasmic organelle of anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing Planctomycetota that localizes the hydrazine-producing anammox catabolic pathway and its energy-conserving membrane reactions.

label: chlorosome
definition: A large light-harvesting antenna organelle of green photosynthetic bacteria in which bacteriochlorophyll aggregates self-assemble inside a lipid envelope and attach to the cytoplasmic membrane through a bacteriochlorophyll a-containing CsmA baseplate.

label: magnetosome
definition: A membrane-bounded organelle of magnetotactic bacteria enclosing a nanocrystal of a magnetic iron mineral — magnetite (Fe3O4) or greigite (Fe3S4). Magnetosomes are invaginations of the cytoplasmic membrane that are filled with iron, and are arranged into a chain along a cytoskeletal filament so that the cell behaves as a swimming compass needle.

label: methane-oxidizing organelle
definition: A cytoplasmic, membrane-bounded organelle in aerobic methanotrophic bacteria, built from intracytoplasmic membranes that house particulate methane monooxygenase and associated electron-transfer proteins for methane catabolism.

label: thylakoid membrane
definition: The pigmented photosynthetic membrane of cyanobacteria and chloroplasts, enriched in photosystems, cytochrome b6f, ATP synthase, plastoquinone and glycolipids, where light-driven electron transport builds the proton motive force for photosynthetic ATP synthesis.

label: bacterial microcompartment
definition: A bacterial protein-shelled organelle in which a selectively permeable polyhedral shell encapsulates pathway enzymes to segregate segments of metabolism from the cytosol.

label: carboxysome
definition: A bacterial microcompartment — a polyhedral, selectively permeable protein shell about 100–200 nm across — that encapsulates RuBisCO and carbonic anhydrase to concentrate CO2 around RuBisCO in cyanobacteria and many chemoautotrophs. Alpha-carboxysomes (cso genes) and beta-carboxysomes (ccm genes) evolved their shells and scaffolds independently.

label: carboxysome shell
definition: The polyhedral protein coat of alpha- and beta-carboxysomes, built from BMC-H, BMC-T, and BMC-P shell proteins that enclose RuBisCO and carbonic anhydrase while controlling metabolite traffic between the lumen and cytosol.

label: encapsulin nanocompartment
definition: A proteinaceous nanocompartment, 24 to 42 nm across, built from a single HK97-fold shell protein that self-assembles into an icosahedron. Cargo enzymes are packaged inside by a short targeting peptide that binds the shell interior; the commonest cargoes are ferritin-like iron-mineralising proteins and peroxidases.

label: ethanolamine degradation polyhedral organelle
definition: An organelle found in bacteria consisting of a proteinaceous coat containing enzymes for the degradation of ethanolamine whose purpose is the protection of the rest of the cell from the toxic acetaldehyde product of the enzyme ethanolamine ammonia lyase.

label: propanediol degradation polyhedral organelle
definition: An organelle found in bacteria consisting of a proteinaceous coat containing enzymes for the degradation of 1,2-propanediol whose purpose is the protection of the rest of the cell from the toxic propionaldehyde product of the enzyme diol dehydratase.

label: nucleoid
definition: The non-membrane-bounded subcellular region in which a bacterial chromosome is compacted and organized with nucleoid-associated proteins while remaining dynamically coupled to transcription and replication.

label: cellulosome
definition: An extracellular membraneless organelle built around scaffoldin and dockerin-bearing enzymes that synergistically degrade insoluble plant-cell-wall polysaccharides.

label: methyl accepting chemotaxis protein complex
definition: The chemoreceptor array: a hexagonal lattice of trimers-of-dimers of methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins, held at the membrane by the CheA kinase and the CheW coupling protein. The array is the cell's sensory organ, and its geometry — a 12 nm hexagonal spacing conserved across bacteria and archaea — is what gives chemotaxis its cooperativity and gain.

label: proteasome core complex
definition: A barrel-shaped self-compartmentalized protease core of proteasomes, built from stacked alpha- and beta-subunit rings that sequester threonine protease active sites in an internal chamber for protein degradation.

label: ribosome
definition: The ribonucleoprotein particle that translates mRNA into protein. The bacterial and archaeal 70S ribosome comprises a small (30S) subunit built on 16S rRNA, which decodes the mRNA, and a large (50S) subunit built on 23S and 5S rRNA, whose 23S rRNA catalyses peptide bond formation. This record details that 70S form and the functional core shared with the larger eukaryotic cytosolic 80S ribosome; it does not enumerate 80S-specific components.

label: ESX-5 type VII secretion system membrane complex
definition: A mycobacterial ESX-5 type VII secretion inner-membrane complex in which EccB5, EccC5, EccD5, EccE5, and MycP5 assemble into a multi-megadalton nanomachine that exports Esx and PE/PPE-family protein substrates.

label: SecYEG translocon complex
definition: A bacterial cytoplasmic-membrane Sec-pathway protein-conducting channel built from SecY, SecE, and SecG, through which unfolded secretory proteins or nascent membrane proteins move during translocation or membrane insertion.

label: TAT protein transport complex
definition: A complex of three proteins integral to the cytoplasmic membrane of bacteria and membranes of organelles derived from bacteria (chloroplasts and mitochondria) involved in membrane transport of folded proteins.

label: type I protein secretion system complex
definition: A Gram-negative bacterial trans-envelope protein secretion complex in which an inner-membrane ABC transporter and membrane-fusion protein recruit a TolC-like outer-membrane channel for one-step export of C-terminal-signal substrates.

label: type II protein secretion system complex
definition: A Gram-negative bacterial envelope-spanning secretion complex in which an inner-membrane platform and ATPase drive pseudopilus-mediated export of folded periplasmic substrates through an outer-membrane secretin.

label: type III protein secretion system complex
definition: The injectisome: a syringe-like envelope-spanning machine that delivers effector proteins from the bacterial cytoplasm directly into a eukaryotic host cell. Rings in the inner and outer membranes surround an export apparatus; an extracellular needle carries the secretion channel to a translocon pore in the host membrane. It is evolutionarily related to the flagellar export apparatus.

label: type IV secretion system complex
definition: A bacterial envelope-spanning secretion complex related to conjugation machines that uses VirB-family channel, pilus, ATPase and coupling-protein subassemblies to translocate DNA and protein substrates.

label: type IX protein secretion system complex
definition: A Bacteroidota trans-envelope secretion nanomachine that couples an inner-membrane PorL/PorM-family motor to PorK/PorN outer-membrane rings and a SprA/Sov translocon to export folded C-terminal-domain-bearing proteins across the outer membrane.

label: type VI protein secretion system complex
definition: A bacterial contractile injection machine whose envelope-spanning membrane complex anchors a baseplate and sheath-wrapped Hcp tube; sheath contraction propels the Hcp/VgrG/PAAR spike and associated effectors out of the cell into target cells.

label: endospore external encapsulating structure
definition: The layered envelope that surrounds a bacterial endospore and gives it its resistance: a thick modified peptidoglycan cortex, a proteinaceous coat of dozens of proteins outside it, and in some species an additional loose exosporium. It encases the dehydrated, mineralised core in which the chromosome is held.
